fx.fx_commentary: The Canadian dollar settled at 0.7148 against the US dollar on June 14, easing 0.40% on the week and 2.1% year-over-year — the move came as the US ceiling held at 3.75% versus the Bank of Canada overnight rate at 2.25%, widening the Fed-BoC differential to approximately 125 basis points following the June 10 BoC hold.121 Commodity flows added pressure as the WTI benchmark fell 11.74% to US$80.58/bbl, reflecting the partial reversal of recent supply-shock premium.37 The euro rose to 1.1600 (+0.87%, +0.1% year-over-year) following the European Central Bank's 25 basis point hike of the deposit facility rate to 2.25% effective June 17 — the first ECB hike since 2023, narrowing the ECB-BoC differential to zero.26 Sterling traded at 1.3408 (-0.14% on the week, -1.6% year-over-year) after the Bank of England's 8-1 vote on April 30 to hold Bank Rate at 3.75%, ahead of the June 18 MPC meeting.28 The dollar against the yen sat at 160.1850 (+0.12%) and against the offshore yuan at 6.7600 (-0.08% on the week, -1.8% year-over-year).37 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties the CAD/USD level to 358 active Canadian manufacturing projects ($82.5B aggregate) priced against US-denominated capital equipment.37 If the loonie holds at current levels through the third quarter, the 358 manufacturing projects would face landed-cost pressure on imported machinery inputs flagged in 2025 capex intentions.11

yieldCurve.yield_commentary: The Government of Canada yield curve held a normal slope on June 12 with the 2s10s spread at +64 basis points — the 10Y benchmark sat at 3.40% versus the 2Y at 2.76%, after the Bank of Canada's June 10 decision to hold the overnight rate at 2.25% for the second consecutive meeting alongside the June Monetary Policy Report.1 Year-over-year, the 2Y has risen 5 basis points from 2.71%, the 5Y 8 basis points from 2.96% to 3.04%, the 10Y 3 basis points from 3.37%, and the long bond 17 basis points from 3.65% to 3.82%, reflecting greater term-premium pickup at the back end than the front.37 The 5Y benchmark at 3.04% remains the residential mortgage-renewal anchor cited in the June MPR.2 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties the curve to 6,426 active Canadian projects ($1,536.5B aggregate) financed against the GoC term structure, with 257 residential projects ($36.2B) most directly exposed to 5Y pricing for mortgage refinancing.37 If the 5Y benchmark holds above three percent through the third quarter, the 257 residential projects would face renewal pricing 8 basis points wider than the year-ago benchmark, while the 1,497 active infrastructure projects priced off the 10Y would carry roughly 3 basis points of additional carry versus the same window in 2025.37
